title: Permanent inequality for rank-at-most-two matrices
statement:
Let $T$ be a matrix of size $n\times n$, and let $\operatorname{per}(T)$ denote its permanent. Form the $2n\times 2n$ block matrix with every block equal to $T$:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}T&T\\T&T\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**Rank-two permanent inequality.** For any matrix $T$ with rank at most $2$,

$$
\operatorname{per}\begin{pmatrix}T&T\\T&T\end{pmatrix}\leq \binom{2n}{n}\operatorname{per}(T)^2.
$$

The conjecture was proposed as a potentially useful tool in finite free probability. The source describes it as an unproved conjecture motivating the determinantal identity, and does not provide evidence of a resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.02528

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).
source_name: Adam W. Marcus, “A Determinantal Identity for the Permanent of a Rank 2 Matrix”, arXiv:2108.02528 (2021).
